reflections.title: "I Have Set the LORD Always Before Me"

reflect.text: Setting the Lord always before us means welcoming Him into all our thoughts, habits, and daily choices. As Charles Spurgeon observed, keeping God near gives us "the sweetest consolation, and the mightiest influence." When the Lord stands at our right hand to protect, counsel, and aid us, we do not need to tremble before sudden troubles, lies, or fear. We cannot be moved from our safety because our faithful Lord is right beside us to hold us up.

questions: What fragile things are you tempted to build your identity on rather than belonging to God?
What is one practical way you can consciously keep the Lord before your mind as you go about your day?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You for adopting us as Your own children. Help us to fix our thoughts and desires on You rather than on earthly success. Stand at our right hand through every storm so that our faith will not be shaken. Amen.

D5.author: Tim Tebow
D5.work: Knowing Whose You Are Changes Everything

unsupported.text: It takes a conscious and deliberate decision of the mind to keep our eyes on God each day. In this life, our earthly achievements, public status, and material possessions can fall apart very quickly. When our best plans break or unexpected failures strike, we are easily shaken if our identity is tied to those fragile markers. Real, lasting security begins only when we remember whose we are. We belong to God, and His love for His children never changes.
unsupported.problem: Neither D5 nor the Scripture passage states that God's love for His children never changes.

reflections.title: "You Will Not Abandon My Soul"

reflect.text: These words were fulfilled when our Savior Jesus died and rose again. When Jesus left this world and entered the realm of death, He committed His spirit to His Father, trusting that He would not be abandoned in the grave. Because God raised Christ to life, this psalm offers deep comfort to every believer who must walk through seasons of sickness, heavy loss, obedience to conscience, or the darkness of death itself.

We also experience times where our spirits descend very low, and we feel trapped in a dark dungeon of doubt or sorrow. In those painful moments, Charles Spurgeon reminds us that "the star of hope is still in the sky when the night is blackest." God may permit us to feel weak and distressed for a time, but He will never abandon us to total ruin or forget His mercy. Even in our final moments on earth, we are not sinking into nothingness; we are resting safely in the hands of our living Savior.

questions: How does the truth of Jesus rising from the dead encourage you when you feel overwhelmed by sadness or grief?
What helps you remember that God is still near when you cannot see the way ahead?
reflections.prayer: Father, thank You that death could not keep Jesus in the grave. When our spirits sink into sadness and we cannot see our way forward, remind us of Your unbroken mercy. Hold us safely in Your loving care and lead us into Your life and light. Amen.

reflections.title: The Path of Life in God's Presence

reflect.text: In Psalm 16, David finds his full satisfaction in God alone, declaring that apart from the Lord there is no good thing. We often look for joy in seasonal celebrations, human praise, or worldly pleasures, but those temporary things inevitably leave our hearts empty. Earthly treasures cannot secure our future or heal our inner ache. Real delight is found only when we take refuge in the Lord and receive Him as our chosen portion and true home.

David speaks of the path of life that leads to fullness of joy in God's presence. As Collin Hansen explains, this path is not a secret puzzle to solve or a detailed road map of future events. The path of life is Jesus Himself. Walking with Christ does not mean knowing every trouble ahead, but learning to trust His daily presence and guidance. By His death and ascension, Jesus has opened the way and secured our eternal joy at God's right hand forever.

questions: What worldly pleasures or distractions have you recently expected to bring satisfaction that only God can give?
How does looking to Jesus as your path of life help you handle worries about the future?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for showing us the path of life by giving us Yourself. Forgive us when we chase after temporary things that can never satisfy our souls. Fill us today with the lasting peace and joy that come from living in Your presence. Amen.
